preface: A board draws part of a Swift codebase as sticky notes: one note per source file, extension point or plugin (or one card per module), its text the doc comment and declarations. A link between two notes is drawn either as an arrow, which puts the two notes next to each other, or as a small reference chip naming the other note, which lets the two sit far apart. Drawing every link as an arrow turns the board into a ball of mud, so arrows go where the two notes form one idea or feature, and chips go on links that are incidental: plumbing, a utility, a registration or plugin list, a style constant, a shared helper.
ask: The link: <the link>. Is this link more than incidental: are the two notes related, or one idea?
The link: <the link>. Do these two notes form one idea or feature, more than merely being related?
